title: Normalization preserves the literal count
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables, whose literal count is the number of literal occurrences it contains (a leaf literal counting once, and an AND or OR gate counting the total over its children). Converting $c$ to strictly alternating AND/OR normal form preserves this count: both the AND-normal form of $c$ and the OR-normal form of $c$ have the same number of literal occurrences as $c$ itself.
hypotheses_covered: c is a Boolean circuit on n variables
replaced:
For every circuit $c$, both normalizations preserve the literal count:
$(c.\mathrm{toNAnd}).\mathrm{litCount} = c.\mathrm{litCount}$ and
$(c.\mathrm{toNOr}).\mathrm{litCount} = c.\mathrm{litCount}$.
